The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. {"timestamp":"2026-07-04T01:10:37.054Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes, something is up with s6, but I do **not** think the live schema blobs being Btrfs-backed is the direct cause.\n\nWhat I found:\n\n- Live schema/blob authority is still tmpfs:\n  - `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat`\n  - `/dev/shm/live-schema.json`\n  - `/dev/shm/opdbus`\n- There are Btrfs blob/demo mounts:\n  - `/opt/op-dbus/blobs/zeroclaw-gemma4`\n  - `/tmp/blob-demo-gemma`\n- Those Btrfs blob mounts are tiny right now, so they are not the s6 lock cause.\n\nThe active s6 problem is clearer:\n\n- `s6-rc -bDa change` PID `31066` is holding the global s6-rc lock.\n- It is blocked waiting for `wg-netmaker` to go down.\n- `wg-netmaker` is still running as `/usr/local/bin/netclient daemon`, PID `927`.\n- Status is: `up ... want down`.\n- Because of that, `s6-rc` commands fail with `unable to take locks`.\n\nThere is also a log-service bug/noise:\n\n- Many `*-log` services are crashing with:\n  - `s6-log: fatal: invalid notification fd: Bad file descriptor`\n- That matches several log services showing `exitcode 100`.\n\nMemory/OOM context:\n\n- Kernel log shows OOM on July 3, 2026 at 19:37:45.\n- `qdrant` was killed, and `rustc` triggered the OOM path.\n- `/tmp` is tmpfs and currently using about `6.7G`, mostly cargo/check/test dirs.\n- No swap is configured.\n- That can absolutely contribute to OOM, but it is separate from the current s6 lock.\n\nThe likely immediate recovery command is:\n\n```sh\nsudo -n s6-svc -k /run/s6-rc/servicedirs/wg-netmaker\n```\n\nThat should let the pending `s6-rc -bDa change` finish and release the lock. It will kill Netmaker/WireGuard for that service, so only do it if your current access does not depend on that tunnel.\n\n","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":{"entries":[{"path":"MEMORY.md","lineStart":181,"lineEnd":187,"note":"used host s6 sudo and local service validation guidance"},{"path":"MEMORY.md","lineStart":49,"lineEnd":50,"note":"used live schema blob path and shm authority context"}],"rolloutIds":["019f0cb9-cc11-7f63-9f39-80e612bb34a2","019f271f-5f4c-7491-817f-4be3878f2100"]}}}
{"timestamp":"2026-07-04T01:10:37.061Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","id":"msg_0d0731532aeb78de016a485d92e0a081a1a6f1cd0c6a7bb021","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"Yes, something is up with s6, but I do **not** think the live schema blobs being Btrfs-backed is the direct cause.\n\nWhat I found:\n\n- Live schema/blob authority is still tmpfs:\n  - `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat`\n  - `/dev/shm/live-schema.json`\n  - `/dev/shm/opdbus`\n- There are Btrfs blob/demo mounts:\n  - `/opt/op-dbus/blobs/zeroclaw-gemma4`\n  - `/tmp/blob-demo-gemma`\n- Those Btrfs blob mounts are tiny right now, so they are not the s6 lock cause.\n\nThe active s6 problem is clearer:\n\n- `s6-rc -bDa change` PID `31066` is holding the global s6-rc lock.\n- It is blocked waiting for `wg-netmaker` to go down.\n- `wg-netmaker` is still running as `/usr/local/bin/netclient daemon`, PID `927`.\n- Status is: `up ... want down`.\n- Because of that, `s6-rc` commands fail with `unable to take locks`.\n\nThere is also a log-service bug/noise:\n\n- Many `*-log` services are crashing with:\n  - `s6-log: fatal: invalid notification fd: Bad file descriptor`\n- That matches several log services showing `exitcode 100`.\n\nMemory/OOM context:\n\n- Kernel log shows OOM on July 3, 2026 at 19:37:45.\n- `qdrant` was killed, and `rustc` triggered the OOM path.\n- `/tmp` is tmpfs and currently using about `6.7G`, mostly cargo/check/test dirs.\n- No swap is configured.\n- That can absolutely contribute to OOM, but it is separate from the current s6 lock.\n\nThe likely immediate recovery command is:\n\n```sh\nsudo -n s6-svc -k /run/s6-rc/servicedirs/wg-netmaker\n```\n\nThat should let the pending `s6-rc -bDa change` finish and release the lock. It will kill Netmaker/WireGuard for that service, so only do it if your current access does not depend on that tunnel.\n\n<oai-mem-citation>\n<citation_entries>\nMEMORY.md:181-187|note=[used host s6 sudo and local service validation guidance]\nMEMORY.md:49-50|note=[used live schema blob path and shm authority context]\n</citation_entries>\n<rollout_ids>\n019f0cb9-cc11-7f63-9f39-80e612bb34a2\n019f271f-5f4c-7491-817f-4be3878f2100\n</rollout_ids>\n</oai-mem-citation>"}],"phase":"final_answer","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f2aaa-79f3-7b92-87b4-1453e436376f"}}}

std::fs;\nuse std::io::Write;\nuse std::path::Path;\nuse tracing::{info, warn};\n\nconst SUBID_REGISTRY: &str = \"/etc/ghostbridge/subid-registry.json\";\nconst XRAY_ROUTES: &str = \"/dev/shm/xray-routes.json\";\nconst OPENFLOW_ROUTES: &str = \"/dev/shm/openflow-routes.json\";\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize)]\nstruct SubidRegistry {\n    version: u32,\n    entries: Vec<RegistryEntry>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize)]\nstruct RegistryEntry {\n    uuid: String,\n    subid: String,\n    #[serde(rename = \"category\")]\n    category: String,\n    #[serde(rename = \"component_type\")]\n    component_type: String,\n    subject: String,\n    verb: String,\n    version: u8,\n    tags: Vec<String>,\n    subdomains: Vec<String>,\n    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    gemma: Option<GemmaConfig>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize)]\nstruct GemmaConfig {\n    backend: BackendSpec,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize)]\n#[serde(tag = \"type\")]\nenum BackendSpec {\n    #[serde(rename = \"ingress\")]\n    Ingress,\n    #[serde(rename = \"tcp\")]\n    Tcp { host: String, port: u16 },\n    #[serde(rename = \"grpc\")]\n    Grpc {\n        host: String,\n        port: u16,\n        #[serde(rename = \"service_name\")]\n        service_name: String,\n    },\n    #[serde(rename = \"unix\")]\n    Unix { path: String },\n    #[serde(rename = \"dns\")]\n    Dns { host: String, port: u16 },\n    /// Internal metadata entry — not xray-routable, produces no outbound.\n    #[serde(rename = \"file\")]\n    File {\n        #[allow(dead_code)]\n        path: String,\n    },\n    /// Internal service — not xray-routable, produces no outbound.\n    #[serde(rename = \"internal\")]\n    Internal,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\nstruct XrayRoutingMap {\n    version: u32,\n    xray_routes: Vec<XrayRoute>,\n    openflow_rules: Vec<OpenFlowRule>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\nstruct XrayRoute {\n    tag: String,\n    subdomains: Vec<String>,\n    backend: BackendSpec,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\nstruct OpenFlowRule {\n    priority: u16,\n    #[serde(rename = \"match_fields\")]\n    match_fields: HashMap<String, String>,\n    actions: Vec<String>,\n    description: Option<String>,\n}\n\nfn main() -> Result<()> {\n    tracing_subscriber::fmt()\n        .with_env_filter(tracing_subscriber::EnvFilter::from_default_env())\n        .init();\n\n    info!(\"Gemma routing brain starting\");\n\n    let registry = load_registry()?;\n    let routes = derive_routes(&registry);\n\n    write_json(XRAY_ROUTES, &routes)?;\n    write_json(OPENFLOW_ROUTES, &routes)?;\n\n    info!(\n        xray_routes = routes.xray_routes.len(),\n        openflow_rules = routes.openflow_rules.len(),\n        \"Gemma wrote routing artifacts\"\n    );\n\n    // Generate the json-render.dev UI spec gallery (200 unique specs)\n    if let Err(e) = ui_gallery::generate_gallery() {\n        warn!(\"Gemma UI gallery generation failed: {e}\");\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn load_registry() -> Result<SubidRegistry> {\n    let raw = fs::read_to_string(SUBID_REGISTRY)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read subid registry: {SUBID_REGISTRY}\"))?;\n    let parsed: SubidRegistry =\n        serde_json::from_str(&raw).with_context(|| \"failed to parse subid registry as JSON\")?;\n    Ok(parsed)\n}\n\nfn derive_routes(registry: &SubidRegistry) -> XrayRoutingMap {\n    let mut xray_routes = Vec::new();\n    let mut openflow_rules = default_privacy_chain();\n\n    for entry in &registry.entries {\n        let Some(gemma) = &entry.gemma else { continue };\n\n        // Skip non-routable backends — they are metadata (schema files,\n        // internal services) that should not produce xray outbounds.\n        if matches!(\n            gemma.backend,\n            BackendSpec::File { .. } | BackendSpec::Internal\n        ) {\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        let tag = entry\n            .tags\n            .first()\n            .cloned()\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| entry.subject.clone());\n\n        // Skip duplicate tags — first declaration wins.\n        if xray_routes.iter().any(|r: &XrayRoute| r.tag == tag) {\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        let route = XrayRoute {\n            tag: tag.clone(),\n            subdomains: entry.subdomains.clone(),\n            backend: gemma.backend.clone(),\n        };\n        xray_routes.push(route);\n\n        if let Some(rule) = backend_to_openflow_rule(&tag, &gemma.backend) {\n            openflow_rules.push(rule);\n        }\n    }\n\n    XrayRoutingMap {\n        version: 1,\n        xray_routes,\n        openflow_rules,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Default privacy chain flows for the GhostBridge OVS bridge.\n/// These match the conventions in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/privacy_router.rs`.\nfn default_privacy_chain() -> Vec<OpenFlowRule> {\n    vec![\n        OpenFlowRule {\n            priority: 100,\n            match_fields: HashMap::from([(\"in_port\".to_string(), \"gbr_wg\".to_string())]),\n            actions: vec![\"output:gbr_warp\".to_string()],\n            description: Some(\"gbr_wg -> gbr_warp\".to_string()),\n        },\n        OpenFlowRule {\n            priority: 100,\n            match_fields: HashMap::from([(\"in_port\".to_string(), \"gbr_warp\".to_string())]),\n            actions: vec![\"output:gbr_xray\".to_string()],\n            description: Some(\"gbr_warp -> gbr_xray\".to_string()),\n        },\n        OpenFlowRule {\n            priority: 100,\n            match_fields: HashMap::from([(\"in_port\".to_string(), \"gbr_xray\".to_string())]),\n            actions: vec![\"output:gbr_warp\".to_string()],\n            description: Some(\"gbr_xray -> gbr_warp\".to_string()),\n        },\n        OpenFlowRule {\n            priority: 200,\n            match_fields: HashMap::from([(\"dl_type\".to_string(), \"0x0806\".to_string())]),\n            actions: vec![\"arp_responder\".to_string()],\n            description: Some(\"ARP Responder for privacy network\".to_string()),\n        },\n    ]\n}\n\n/// Translate a Gemma backend into an OpenFlow rule for the bridge.\n/// Only TCP/GRPC backends produce IP/Port matchable rules here; Unix sockets\n/// route through the tonic-web gRPC bridge (reflection demuxes) so no OVS\n/// bridge match is needed.\nfn backend_to_openflow_rule(tag: &str, backend: &BackendSpec) -> Option<OpenFlowRule> {\n    let (host, port) = match backend {\n        BackendSpec::Tcp { host, port } => (host.clone(), *port),\n        BackendSpec::Grpc { host, port, .. } => (host.clone(), *port),\n        BackendSpec::Ingress\n        | BackendSpec::Unix { .. }\n        | BackendSpec::Dns { .. }\n        | BackendSpec::File { .. }\n        | BackendSpec::Internal => return None,\n    };\n\n    let mut match_fields = HashMap::new();\n    match_fields.insert(\"dl_type\".to_string(), \"0x0800\".to_string());\n    match_fields.insert(\"nw_proto\".to_string(), \"6\".to_string()); // TCP\n    match_fields.insert(\"nw_dst\".to_string(), host.clone());\n    match_fields.insert(\"tp_dst\".to_string(), port.to_string());\n\n    Some(OpenFlowRule {\n        priority: 150,\n        match_fields,\n        actions: vec![\"output:ovsbr0-mgmt\".to_string()],\n        description: Some(format!(\"Gemma: {tag} -> host backend {host}:{port}\")),\n    })\n}\n\nfn write_json<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P, value: &XrayRoutingMap) -> Result<()> {\n    let tmp = format!(\"{}.tmp\", path.as_ref().display());\n    let mut f =\n        fs::File::create(&tmp).with_context(|| format!(\"failed to create tmp file: {tmp}\"))?;\n    let json =\n        serde_json::to_string_pretty(value).with_context(|| \"failed to serialize routing map\")?;\n    f.write_all(json.as_bytes())\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to write tmp file: {tmp}\"))?;\n    f.sync_data()\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to sync tmp file: {tmp}\"))?;\n    fs::rename(&tmp, path.as_ref())\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to rename {tmp} to {}\", path.as_ref().display()))?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n--- Cargo ---\n[package]\nname = \"op-gemma\"\nversion.workspace = true\nedition.workspace = true\nauthors.workspace = true\nlicense.workspace = If an attacker controls or influences these parameters, they can inject JSON control characters (e.g. `\", \"injected_key\": \"injected_value\", \"dummy\": \"`) into the output file `/dev/shm/xray-ghostbridge.json`. This allows an attacker to manipulate DNS routes, tproxy settings, or force xray connections to route traffic to an attacker-controlled gateway.\ncrates/audits/op-identity/10_10_Documentation_Completeness.md:77:  Both files live in `/dev/shm`, which is a world-writable directory. Because `File::create` follows symlinks, a local, unprivileged attacker can create a symbolic link at `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat.tmp` or `/dev/shm/xray-ghostbridge.json.tmp` pointing to any critical system file (e.g., `/etc/passwd`, `/etc/shadow`, or systemd service units). When the privileged `op-identity` process (which executes root-level `wg` and `incus` wrapper commands) writes the identity sled or Xray configuration, it will overwrite the target file, leading to system corruption or immediate privilege escalation.\ncrates/audits/op-identity/10_10_Documentation_Completeness.md:93:  `File::create` opens the target file with default permissions (typically `0644` modified by the process umask, resulting in world-readable files on standard system configurations). Since the output directory is the shared memory partition `/dev/shm`, **any unprivileged local user or container on the system can read `/dev/shm/xray-ghostbridge.json` and extract the plaintext Xray REALITY private key (`privateKey`).**\ncrates/audits/op-identity/10_10_Documentation_Completeness.md:95:  Set the file permissions of `/dev/shm/xray-ghostbridge.json` (and its `.tmp` builder) strictly to read/write by owner only (`0600`). In Rust, this should be done using `std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt`:\ncrates/audits/op-identity/12_12_Integration_Points_Consumers.md:16:The `op-identity` crate does not spin up its own HTTP or gRPC server directly. Instead, its `schema_bridge.rs` module manages the network border by dynamically generating an Xray core JSON configuration (`/dev/shm/xray-ghostbridge.json`) which spawns network-level interceptors and endpoints:\ncrates/audits/op-identity/08_08_Performance_Allocation_And_Memory.md:12:1. **Sled Storage Location**: The `IdentitySled` is stored on a `tmpfs` volume (`/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat`). If `/dev/shm` is mounted with the `noexec` option, it prevents binary execution from the mount but still permits memory-mapping files. However, because `/dev/shm` is world-writable on standard Linux configurations, the files `plugin_schema.dat`, `snowball_session.log`, and `xray-ghostbridge.json` are exposed to symlink hijacking, local tampering, and unauthorized manipulation by other local users.\ncrates/audits/op-identity/08_08_Performance_Allocation_And_Memory.md:50:  * `/dev/shm/xray-ghostbridge.json`\ncrates/audits/op-identity/09_09_Test_Coverage_Examples.md:58:  The paths `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat`, `/dev/shm/snowball_session.log`, and `/dev/shm/xray-ghostbridge.json` are hardcoded in a globally writable directory (`/dev/shm`). \ncrates/audits/op-identity/01_01_Architecture_Module_Map.md:208:Because this configuration is written to `/dev/shm/xray-ghostbridge.json` and executed with system privileges, structural manipulation of this JSON could allow malicious actors to rewrite proxy rules, inject arbitrary endpoints, or alter DNS endpoints.\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f2ab9-ebde-7ee1-9424-2a4e5bf27585"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-07-04T01:26:52.587Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_vmcaK2yDYoO9OrybVyJy7wid","output":"Chunk ID: 2234cf\nWall time: 0.0001 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1494\nOutput:\n#!/bin/sh\nset -eu\n\nPATH=\"${PATH:-/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin}\"\n\nGEMMA_BIN=\"${GEMMA_BIN:-/usr/local/bin/op-gemma}\"\nSHUTTLE_BIN=\"${SHUTTLE_BIN:-/usr/local/bin/op-identity-shuttle}\"\n\nif [ -f /etc/ghostbridge/xray.env ]; then\n    . /etc/ghostbridge/xray.env\nfi\n\necho \"gemma: generating subid → tag → xray + OpenFlow rules\"\n\"$GEMMA_BIN\"\n\necho \"gemma: running identity shuttle to regenerate xray config\"\n\"$SHUTTLE_BIN\"\n\necho \"gemma: ready\"\n#!/bin/sh\nexec 2>&1\nset -eu\n\nPATH=\"${PATH:-/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin}\"\n\nGEMMA_BIN=\"${GEMMA_BIN:-/usr/local/bin/op-gemma}\"\nSHUTTLE_BIN=\"${SHUTTLE_BIN:-/usr/local/bin/op-identity-shuttle}\"\nGEMMA_INTERVAL_SECONDS=\"${GEMMA_INTERVAL_SECONDS:-300}\"\n\nif [ -f /etc/ghostbridge/xray.env ]; then\n    . /etc/ghostbridge/xray.env\nfi\n\nwhile :; do\n    \"$GEMMA_BIN\"\n\n    \"$SHUTTLE_BIN\"\n\n    sleep \"$GEMMA_INTERVAL_SECONDS\"\ndone\n#!/bin/bash\n# deploy-blob-gemma4.sh\n#\n# Deploys the complete gemma4+zeroclaw \"blob\" as a btrfs subvolume.\n#\n# Architectural reality (per this system):\n# - The **blob itself** is a self-contained btrfs subvolume (or filesystem).\n#   It can be cloned, mounted as a subvol, sent over the wire, or used to extend\n#   other filesystems. This is why btrfs is a big part of the blob story.\n# - **Mutations** (changing live state, configs, etc.) never happen by directly\n#   writing files inside the blob from the running services. All mutation happens\n#   exclusively over D-Bus (zbus), gRPC, and JSON-RPC. This avoids mutation loops.\n# - On host, the gemma4 blob provides a complete, mountable unit containing:\n#     - frozen zeroclaw state + manifests\n#     - the gemma4 model reference / bind\n#     - the recovered PluginObjectBlob / reflection metadata\n#     - any supporting projection files\n#\n# The running zeroclaw surfaces (dbus object + gRPC) project / reflect the blob\n# contents at runtime. The subvolume is the distributable/frozen unit.\n#\n# Incus note: `incus list` on this host is currently authoritative except for\n# the unused \"netmaker-exporter\".\n#\n# Usage:\n#   sudo ./deploy/deploy-blob-gemma4.sh\n#   (or DEST=... BTRFS_ROOT=...)\n\nset -euo pipefail\n\nBLOB_NAME=${1:-zeroclaw-gemma4-gemma4}\nBTRFS_ROOT=${BTRFS_ROOT:-/mnt/btrfs-root}\nSUBVOL=\"@blob-${BLOB_NAME}\"\nDEST=${DEST:-/opt/op-dbus/blobs/${BLOB_NAME}}\n\necho \"=== Gemma4 Zeroclaw Btrfs Blob Deployment ===\"\necho \"Creating btrfs subvolume for the blob (mountable unit): ${SUBVOL}\"\n\nsudo mkdir -p \"$BTRFS_ROOT\"\nif ! sudo btrfs subvolume show \"${BTRFS_ROOT}/${SUBVOL}\" &>/dev/null; then\n  sudo btrfs subvolume create \"${BTRFS_ROOT}/${SUBVOL}\" || true\nfi\n\nsudo mkdir -p \"$DEST\"\nsudo mount --bind \"${BTRFS_ROOT}/${SUBVOL}\" \"$DEST\" 2>/dev/null || true\n\necho \"[blob] subvolume ready at $DEST (btrfs subvol: $SUBVOL)\"\n\n# Live local model requirement\nOLLAMA_URL=${OLLAMA_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:11434}\nMODEL=${MODEL:-gemma4:12b}\n\nif ! curl -fsS --max-time 3 \"$OLLAMA_URL/api/tags\" > /dev/null 2>&1; then\n  echo \"WARNING: Ollama not responding at $OLLAMA_URL (model bind will be recorded anyway)\"\nelse\n  if ! curl -fsS --max-time 5 \"$OLLAMA_URL/api/tags\" | grep -q \"$MODEL\"; then\n    echo \"Pulling $MODEL into host ollama...\"\n    curl -X POST -d \"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"$MODEL\\\"}\" \"$OLLAMA_URL/api/pull\" || true\n  fi\nfi\n\n# Write the contract and snapshot directly into the btrfs-backed blob dir\n# (this is population of the frozen unit, not runtime mutation of live state)\necho \"[blob] writing frozen manifests into the subvol...\"\nsudo tee \"$DEST/MANIFEST.blob.json\" > /dev/null <<'MANIFEST'\n{\n  \"kind\": \"zeroclaw-gemma4-ollama\",\n  \"model\": \"gemma4:12b\",\n  \"provider\": \"ollama\",\n  \"router\": \"gemma4\",\n  \"btrfs_subvol\": \"@blob-zeroclaw-gemma4\",\n  \"note\": \"This directory is the root of a btrfs subvolume. It can be mounted, cloned, or used to extend filesystems. All live mutations to zeroclaw state and routing occur exclusively over D-Bus + gRPC + JSON-RPC. No direct file mutation from the services.\"\n}\nMANIFEST\n\nsudo tee \"$DEST/OBJECT_BLOB.json\" > /dev/null <<'OBJ'\n{\n  \"plugin_id\": \"zeroclaw\",\n  \"schema_version\": \"1.0.0\",\n  \"schema_source\": \"recovered + live PluginSchema from current_state (schemars+uniform)\",\n  \"dbus\": {\n    \"bus_name\": \"org.opdbus.v1.plugins\",\n    \"object_path\": \"/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw\",\n    \"interface_name\": \"org.opdbus.v1.Plugin\"\n  },\n  \"grpc\": {\n    \"package\": \"operation.plugin.v1\",\n    \"service_name\": \"operation.plugin.v1.ZeroclawPluginMethods\"\n  },\n  \"methods\": [\n    {\"schema_name\": \"query_current_state\", \"grpc_name\": \"QueryCurrentState\", \"subid\": \"obs.service.zeroclaw.state\"},\n    {\"schema_name\": \"chat\", \"grpc_name\": \"Chat\", \"subid\": \"mut.service.zeroclaw.chat\"}\n  ],\n  \"gemma4_blob\": {\n    \"model\": \"gemma4:12b\",\n    \"provider\": \"ollama\",\n    \"local_endpoint\": \"http://127.0.0.1:11434\",\n    \"role\": \"context_aware_allocator\",\n    \"mountable_as_subvol\": true\n  }\n}\nOBJ\n\n# Also drop a copy of current declared state for the frozen unit\nsudo tee \"$DEST/state_snapshot.json\" > /dev/null <<'STATE'\n{\"status\":\"active\",\"selected_provider\":\"ollama\",\"selected_model\":\"gemma4\",\"blob\":{\"kind\":\"zeroclaw-gemma4-ollama\",\"status\":\"complete\",\"btrfs\":true}}\nSTATE\n\n# Optionally bind the actual ollama model store (read-only, to keep the blob self-contained without duplication)\nOLLAMA_MODELS=${OLLAMA_MODELS:-/var/lib/ollama/models}\nif [ -d \"$OLLAMA_MODELS\" ]; then\n  sudo mkdir -p \"$DEST/models\"\n  sudo mount --bind --read-only \"$OLLAMA_MODELS\" \"$DEST/models\" 2>/dev/null || true\n  echo \"[blob] models bind-mounted (ro) into subvol\"\nfi\n\necho \"[blob] populated: $DEST\"\necho \"Subvolume can now be mounted elsewhere, cloned (btrfs send/receive), etc.\"\necho \"The live surfaces in zeroclaw (DBus + gRPC) will report this blob as complete when the mount is present.\"\n\necho \"Current incus containers (authoritative except netmaker-exporter):\"\nincus list 2>/dev/null || echo \"incus not available in this context\"\n\nls -l \"$DEST\"\necho\necho \"Blob subvolume ready. Activate / project via normal D-Bus + op-projection paths.\"","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f2ab9-ebde-7ee1-9424-2a4e5bf27585"}}}

}\n            \"--help\" | \"-h\" => {\n                print_help();\n                std::process::exit(0);\n            }\n            other => anyhow::bail!(\"unknown argument: {other}\"),\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(Args { env_file })\n}\n\nfn print_help() {\n    println!(\n        \"op-identity-shuttle\\n\\n\\\nUsage:\\n  op-identity-shuttle [--env-file PATH]\\n\\n\\\nOptions:\\n  --env-file fs::read_to_string(path)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read env file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n    for line in contents.lines() {\n        let trimmed = line.trim();\n        if The final\n/// catch-all rule sends unmatched ingress traffic to the grpc-bridge, matching\n/// the historical fallback behavior.\n#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]\nfn build_xray_config(\n    footprint: &str,\n    trace_id: &str,\n    nextdns_profile: &str,\n    uuid: &str,\n    private_key: &str,\n    short_id: &str,\n    sockets: &[SocketEntry],\n    routes: &[XrayRoute],\n) -> String {\n    // Gemma-supplied routes; empty when Gemma has not yet run.\n    let mut routes = routes.to_vec();\n    let mut seen_tags: HashSet<String> = routes.iter().map(|r| r.tag.clone()).collect();\n\n    // Merge legacy UNIX_SOCKET_ENDPOINTS entries for backward compatibility.\n    for socket in sockets {\n        let tag = socket.label.clone();\n        if seen_tags.contains(&tag) {\n            continue;\n        }\n        seen_tags.insert(tag.clone());\n        routes.push(XrayRoute {\n            tag,\n            subdomains: vec![socket.domain.clone()],\n            backend: GemmaBackend::Unix {\n                path: socket.path.clone(),\n            },\n        });\n    }\n\n    // Outbound for each route that has a backend (ingress tags have none).\n    let route_outbounds: String = routes\n        .iter()\n        .filter_map(|r| route_to_outbound(footprint, trace_id, r))\n        .collect();\n\n    // Subdomain routing rules for each route with subdomains and a real backend.\n    // Ingress-only entries (e.g. xray-tls/xray-reality) describe the listener,\n    // not a destination, so no routing rule is emitted for them.\n    let route_rules: String = routes\n        .iter()\n        .filter_map(|r| {\n            if r.subdomains.is_empty() || matches!(r.backend, GemmaBackend::Ingress) {\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f2ab9-ebde-7ee1-9424-2a4e5bf27585"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-07-04T01:30:21.564Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call","id":"fc_0681043a95224b16016a48623a8188819cb7dc03e9de16706b","name":"exec_command","arguments":"{\"cmd\":\"sudo -n sh -c '\\nset -eu\\nfile=/etc/s6/sv/op-dbus/run\\nbackup=/etc/s6/sv/op-dbus/run.bak.stepdown-$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)\\ncp -p \\\"$file\\\" \\\"$backup\\\"\\ntmp=$(mktemp)\\nawk '\\n  { print }\\n  /^export DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=/ && !done {\\n    print \\\"if [ -f /etc/ghostbridge/zeroclaw.env ]; then\\\"\\n    print \\\"    set -a\\\"\\n    print \\\"    . /etc/ghostbridge/zeroclaw.env\\\"\\n    print \\\"    set +a\\\"\\n    print \\\"fi\\\"\\n    done=1\\n  }\\n' \\\"$file\\\" > \\\"$tmp\\\"\\ninstall -m 0755 -o root -g root \\\"$tmp\\\" \\\"$file\\\"\\nrm -f \\\"$tmp\\\"\\nprintf \\\"%s\\\\n\\\" \\\"$backup\\\"\\n'\",\"workdir\":\"/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto\",\"yield_time_ms\":10000,\"max_output_tokens\":12000}","call_id":"call_W3bl0RftUvR0mLgraBi69oEy","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f2ab9-ebde-7ee1-9424-2a4e5bf27585"}}}

In `main.rs:164`, these values are parsed and injected into forwarded gRPC requests as standard `x-ghostbridge-footprint` and `x-ghostbridge-trace-id` headers. Because `/dev/shm` is typically world-writable or writable by any local process, the file `plugin_schema.dat` can be modified or created by unprivileged local processes.\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/17_17_DBus_IPC_Attack_Surface.md:45:* **Exploitation Scenario**: A malicious local user or compromised local application on the host machine overwrites `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` with a forged WireGuard public key and trace ID. The proxy reads this file, sets `is_valid` to `true`, and injects the forged identity headers into all subsequent control plane gRPC requests forwarded to `op-dbus`, effectively spoofing the identity of other authorized network nodes or peers.\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/17_17_DBus_IPC_Attack_Surface.md:53:* **Description**: In `sled.rs`, `SledSnapshot::read()` uses `memmap2` to map `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` with a hardcoded length of `SLED_SIZE` (208 bytes). However, the mapping is created and read from without pre-validating that the physical file size is at least `SLED_SIZE` bytes. Furthermore, the file is not locked.\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/17_17_DBus_IPC_Attack_Surface.md:54:* **Exploitation Scenario**: An attacker truncates `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` to 0 bytes. Because `SIGBUS` is unhandled, this results in a sudden, unrecoverable denial-of-service crash of the proxy process.\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/17_17_DBus_IPC_Attack_Surface.md:108:   * `crates/op-mcp-proxy/src/sled.rs:21` implements `SledSnapshot` to mirror raw C-struct structures located in `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` without formal protobuf schemas or versioning indicators:\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/09_09_Test_Coverage_Examples.md:31:    *   `crates/op-mcp-proxy/src/sled.rs:21-75`: The layout of `plugin_schema.dat` is parsed via raw byte offset slices (e.g., `&bytes[96..160]`). This layout mirrors an external struct from another crate without any schema version negotiation or validation, risking severe memory misalignment if either crate changes layout.\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/09_09_Test_Coverage_Examples.md:71:    If `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` is missing, corrupted, or has `is_valid = false`, `use_xray` silently becomes `false`. Because memory mapping represents the file directly in the virtual memory space of the process, if another process truncates or changes the file size of `plugin_schema.dat` while `op-mcp-proxy` is running, any read of the slice will immediately trigger a `SIGBUS` signal, terminating the proxy process.\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/16_16_Improvement_Suggestions.md:3:2. **Suggestion:** Replace Ad-Hoc Offsets in Sled Slicing with a Shared Schema Struct | **Rationale:** The zero-copy memory reader maps `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` and parses binary data using ad-hoc hardcoded slices and byte offsets (e.g. `&bytes[192..208]`). This violates the schema-as-code discipline. If the producer (`op-identity::schema_bridge`) changes its internal struct alignment or layout, this reader will silently read corrupted offsets. Both crates should share a versioned, common struct annotated with `#[repr(C)]` or serialize via a shared versioned schema protocol. | **Example:** `crates/op-mcp-proxy/src/sled.rs:49`\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/08_08_Performance_Allocation_And_Memory.md:11:| `SledSnapshot::read()` maps `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` | `crates/op-mcp-proxy/src/sled.rs:35` | `ro` | **SIGBUS Crash**: Maps a file on `tmpfs`. If the file is truncated concurrently, accessing the mapped slice will trigger a SIGBUS and crash the process. Lacks validation of structural bounds. |\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/07_07_Security_Unsafe_Surface.md:11:*   **Analysis**: Memory-mapping a file is inherently unsafe because the underlying file can be truncated or modified by other processes or threads, which violates Rust's memory aliasing and reference validity guarantees. There is no `// SAFETY:` block explaining why this operation is safe, how access to `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` is synchronized, or how the application prevents `SIGBUS` crashes if the file is truncated.\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/07_07_Security_Unsafe_Surface.md:128:*   **Details**: The identity exchange between the background identity component and the proxy relies on reading a custom `#[repr(C)]` layout directly from shared memory `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat`.\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/07_07_Security_Unsafe_Surface.md:165:*   **Impact**: The application memory-maps the file `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` which lives in shared memory (`/dev/shm`). If any other process on the host (including unprivileged local users, depending on file permissions) truncates this file while the proxy is running, any read access to the slice references (e.g. `bytes[..SLED_SIZE]`) will immediately trigger a `SIGBUS` signal. Because `op-mcp-proxy` does not register a custom signal handler to catch and recover from `SIGBUS`, this will cause an ungraceful, unlogged crash (Denial of Service).\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/15_15_License_Compliance.md:53:  pub const SLED_PATH: &str = \"/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat\";\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/15_15_License_Compliance.md:100:  The proxy reads memory-mapped configuration data from shared memory (`/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat`):\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/15_15_License_Compliance.md:107:  If a local attacker or concurrent process truncates or changes the size of `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` after the mapping is established, reading from the `bytes` slice triggers a kernel page fault, sending a `SIGBUS` signal to the process and crashing it instantly.\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/06_06_Async_Concurrency_Model.md:87:In `crates/op-mcp-proxy/src/sled.rs:13-25`, the binary representation of `plugin_schema.dat` is parsed using hardcoded byte slices:\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/06_06_Async_Concurrency_Model.md:118:  The identity sled file is read directly from `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat`. This is a highly brittle, unversioned binary contract. Any modification to the `IdentitySled` struct in the upstream `op-identity` crate will silently corrupt data read by this proxy without compiler diagnostics. Instead of failing safely and refusing to start, the program initiates the `DirectLLM` companion using `None` as the proxy:\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/05_05_Error_Handling_Result_Patterns.md:105:*   **Flag:** The layout of the memory-mapped file `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` is parsed using manual byte slicing (e.g., `&bytes[0..32]`, `bytes[32..40]`). This represents an ad-hoc, unversioned binary structure that mirrors a raw C memory layout. It will silently corrupt data or fail to parse if the producer structure shifts. This should be defined as a versioned Protocol Buffer schema.\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/05_05_Error_Handling_Result_Patterns.md:151:*   **Risk Analysis:** `memmap2` is marked `unsafe` because the underlying file can be truncated or modified by another process while mapped. If `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` is truncated or modified by the system or another process while this proxy is reading from it, a `SIGBUS` signal (bus error) will be triggered. This causes an immediate, uncatchable crash of the proxy process.\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/13_13_Observability_Logging.md:108:* **Impact**: Unsynchronized access to the shared-memory file `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` via `Mmap` results in undefined behavior (UB) under Rust's aliasing rules.\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/12_12_Integration_Points_Consumers.md:16:*   It reads local identity data directly from a memory-mapped file (`/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat`) rather than making D-Bus IPC calls.\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/12_12_Integration_Points_Consumers.md:40:    The zero-copy reader maps `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` using `memmap2::MmapOptions` with a hardcoded length of `208` bytes:\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/11_11_Configuration_Feature_Flags.md:89:* **`/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` (`crates/op-mcp-proxy/src/sled.rs:21`)**\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/10_10_Documentation_Completeness.md:133:*   **Impact**: The file mapping occurs over `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat`. Because memory-mapping a file does not prevent truncation by other processes on the system, any local unprivileged process that can write to `/dev/shm` can truncate this file to 0 bytes. If the file is truncated while `op-mcp-proxy` reads from the `mmap` reference, the OS will raise a `SIGBUS` signal, resulting in an uncatchable immediate crash of the proxy.\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/04_04_Data_Structures_State_Model.md:75:* **Exploitability**: Because `/dev/shm` is a standard, temporary, world-writable memory directory on Linux, any local unprivileged process can write, overwrite, or delete `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat`. By truncating or deleting this file, an attacker can reliably trigger the proxy to silently bypass the SOCKS5 proxy and leak the user's IP address, DNS requests, and sensitive queries over the plain public internet. This constitutes a severe, exploitable fail-open design flaw.\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/04_04_Data_Structures_State_Model.md:83:* **Description**: The binary reads `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` by memory mapping a fixed 208-byte segment inside `unsafe`:\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/04_04_Data_Structures_State_Model.md:90:* **Exploitability**: Since `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` is located in the world-writable `/dev/shm` directory, any unprivileged local process can truncate the file. Once truncated, the next time the proxy executes `SledSnapshot::read()` (which happens on every incoming stdin loop iteration), dereferencing `bytes` will immediately crash the daemon with `SIGBUS`. There are no signal handlers or safety boundaries preventing this crash.\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/03_03_Dependency_Feature_Audit.md:49:| `memmap2` (\"sled\") | `crates/op-mcp-proxy/src/sled.rs:25` | **Shared Memory (Zero-copy IPC)**: Reads `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` representing the identity memory structure. | **Violation**: Directly maps raw shared-memory bytes. Highly vulnerable to UB and SIGBUS crashes. (See Finding 1). |\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/03_03_Dependency_Feature_Audit.md:86:The proxy maps a local file in shared memory (`/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat`) into its memory space via `memmap2` and casts it to a Rust byte slice (`&[u8]`):\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/03_03_Dependency_Feature_Audit.md:95:1.  **Aliasing Violation (Undefined Behavior)**: `bytes` is a shared immutable reference (`&[u8]`). Rust compiler optimizations assume that the memory pointed to by `&[u8]` cannot change. However, because `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` can be mutated concurrently by other processes (e.g., `op-identity`), the memory can change, leading to compiler-induced undefined behavior (UB), data races, and memory corruption.\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/03_03_Dependency_Feature_Audit.md:96:2.  **SIGBUS Crash (Exploitable Denial of Service)**: If any local process (even an unprivileged one sharing the `/dev/shm` namespace) truncates the `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` file to a size smaller than `SLED_SIZE` after mapping, any future read access to `bytes` will raise a `SIGBUS` signal. Because `SIGBUS` is not caught by the Rust runtime, the `op-mcp-proxy` process will crash instantly.\ncrates/audits/op-introspection/13_13_Observability_Logging.md:86:* **Risk**: Inside `introspect_and_persist`, the code receives a raw, schema-less `simd_json::OwnedValue` from `self.introspect()`, writes it as raw JSON text directly to the blockchain's BTRFS state subvolume (`bc.write_state`), and commits its raw cryptographic hash to the block ledger. Because this state is stored without a defined schema contract, there is no structural verification that the persisted metadata matches the exact criteria expected by recovery plugins. \ncrates/audits/op-plugins/16_16_Risk_Register_Tech_Debt.md:4:| **High** | **Tokio Thread Deadlock via Synchronous `blocking_read`**<br>Invoking `blocking_read()` on an `AsyncRwLock` inside a synchronous execution pathway (`state_hash`). If the lock is contested by an active write lock on a tokio-managed executor thread, this blocks the entire OS worker thread, leading to scheduler starvation and immediate deadlocks. | `crates/op-plugins/src/dynamic_loading.rs:403` | Never mix `blocking_read()` with asynchronous code paths on the same lock. Convert `state_hash` to be an asynchronous method (`async fn state_hash`), or use a synchronous lock library like `parking_lot::RwLock` for fields that do not require async scheduling. |\ncrates/audits/op-plugins/14_14_Build_CI_Workspace_Wiring.md:15:    *   `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs:1-600`: The entire file consists of manual, programmatic Rust definitions using a custom `PluginSchema::builder` pattern (e.g., `incus_plugin_schema` and `openflow_plugin_schema`). This violates the \"source-of-truth\" principle of Schema-as-Code, since contracts are tightly coupled to Rust-specific builders.\ncrates/audits/op-plugins/16_16_Improvement_Suggestions.md:17:9. **Suggestion**: Migrate plain JSON file storage to a transactional database backend (such as CozoDB with Sled or SQLite) or perform atomic writes via a temporary file rename pattern. | **Rationale**: Overwriting files directly with `tokio::fs::write` is susceptible to partial writes and data corruption if a power failure or system crash occurs mid-write. Initialize Schema Engine + discover plugin schemas (writes to shm).\n    29\t    let mut schema_engine = SchemaEngine::new();\n    30\t\n    31\t    let plugin_reader = match SystemPluginReader::new().await {\n    32\t        Ok(reader) => reader,\n    33\t        Err(error) => {\n    34\t            warn!(\n    35\t                error = %error,\n    36\t                \"Failed to initialize plugin reader; continuing with empty schema catalog\"\n    37\t            );\n    38\t            SystemPluginReader::empty()\n    39\t        }\n    40\t    };\n    41\t\n    42\t    let projection_schemas = plugin_reader.projection_schemas();\n    43\t    let schema_map: HashMap<String, PluginSchema> = projection_schemas\n    44\t        .iter()\n    45\t        .map(|schema| (schema.name.clone(), schema.clone()))\n    46\t        .collect();\n    47\t\n    48\t    for schema in projection_schemas {\n    49\t        register_schema_if_missing(&mut schema_engine, schema)?;\n    50\t    }\n    51\t\n    52\t    info!(\n    53\t        schemas = schema_engine.list_schemas().len(),\n    54\t        \"Schema catalog published to shm\"\n    55\t    );\n    56\t\n    57\t    // 2. Initialize D-Bus server (owns org.opdbus.v1.plugins, root interface\n    58\t    //    at /org/opdbus/v1/plugins is always present for introspection).\n    59\t    let dbus_server = ProjectionDbusServer::new_with_schemas(schema_map.clone())\n    60\t        .await\n    61\t        .context(\"failed to start projection D-Bus server\")?;\n    62\t\n    63\t    // 3. Initial tree sync: mount from shm (mutations) then seed all known\n    64\t    //    plugin roots from the schema catalog so the tree is never empty.\n    65\t    dbus_server.sync_from_shm().await?;\n    66\t\n    67\t    let known_plugins: Vec<String> = schema_map.keys().cloned().collect();\n    68\t    dbus_server.seed_plugin_roots(&known_plugins).await?;\n    69\t\n    70\t    let count = dbus_server.object_count().await;\n    71\t    info!(\n    72\t        objects = count,\n    73\t        plugins = known_plugins.len(),\n    74\t        \"Initial tree sync complete\"\n    75\t    );\n    76\t\n    77\t    // 4. Initialize JSON-stream server (for WebSocket clients).\n    78\t    let mut stream_server = ProjectionStreamServer::new();\n    79\t    stream_server.start(8082)?;\n    80\t\n    81\t    // 5. Run forever. The tree is derived on-demand via the `refresh()` D-Bus\n    82\t    //    method on the ProjectionRoot interface. No gRPC, no polling.\n    83\t    info!(\"Projection server ready — tree syncs on refresh() D-Bus call or restart\");\n    84\t    tokio::signal::ctrl_c().await?;\n    85\t\n    86\t    Ok(())\n    87\t}\n    88\t\n    89\tfn register_schema_if_missing(\n    90\t    schema_engine: &mut SchemaEngine,\n    91\t    schema: PluginSchema,\n    92\t) -> Result<()> {\n    93\t    if schema_engine.has_valid_schema(&schema.name) {\n    94\t        return Ok(());\n    95\t    }\n    96\t\n    97\t    let schema_name = schema.name.clone();\n    98\t    schema_engine\n    99\t        .register_schema(schema)\n   100\t        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to register projection schema '{}'\", schema_name))?;\n   101\t    Ok(())\n   102\t}\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f2ac3-ca9d-7e71-83d4-38537dce806c"}}}

derive_child_paths(plugin_id, &self.state_dir, &route.properties)\n   206\t                    .into_iter()\n   207\t                    .map(|segments| {\n   208\t                        (\n   209\t                            build_child_path(plugin_id, &segments),\n   210\t                            plugin_id.clone(),\n   211\t                            segments,\n   212\t                        )\n   213\t                    })\n   214\t                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n   215\t            })\n   216\t            .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n   217\t        drop(routes);\n   218\t\n let mut current = self.child_objects.write().await;\n   225\t        for stale in current\n   226\t            .iter()\n   227\t            .filter(|path| !desired_paths.contains(*path))\n   228\t Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * {"timestamp":"2026-07-04T01:39:43.028Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes. The repo confirms that.\n\n`op-blob` can write blobs to `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs` via [catalog.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-blob/src/catalog.rs:23), and the bridge has a side-effect writer in [grpc_server.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/grpc_server.rs:484).\n\nBut that does **not** make the bridge a full projection replacement. The bridge only writes a blob after it already receives a `PluginSchema` and runs `register_plugin_methods`. The missing part is the producer/materializer that turns the real plugin schema set into active SHM blobs at boot.\n\nThe clearest tell is [op-projection/src/blob.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-projection/src/blob.rs:85): it says the integration hook is still to call `blobify_plugin_schema` from `op-grpc-bridge` or `op-projection` and push blobs into `ActiveReflectionCatalog`. That is scaffold/handoff language.\n\nAlso `opblob` itself only has `demo-seal`, `inspect`, `catalog`, `btrfs-seal`, and `keygen` in [opblob.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-blob/src/bin/opblob.rs:4). There is no real `seal-plugin zeroclaw` / `seal-catalog-from-op-plugins` command.\n\nCurrent SHM state matches that: `/dev/shm/opdbus` does not exist, so no active blob catalog is being materialized. `live-schema.json` is still around, but per your correction that should not be the authority.\n\nSo the accurate status is: **blob crate exists, bridge has partial blob persistence, projection/materialization was left unwired.** The next real fix is one narrow materializer path that writes real `PluginSchema` blobs into `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs`, not more `live-schema.json` chasing.\n\n","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":{"entries":[{"path":"MEMORY.md","lineStart":48,"lineEnd":54,"note":"blob authority and incomplete end to end blob runtime context"},{"path":"MEMORY.md","lineStart":181,"lineEnd":187,"note":"local s6 deploy and validation patterns"}],"rolloutIds":[]}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-07-04T01:40:53.695Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"It can. That is probably the right shape.\n\nThe reason it **doesn’t today** is implementation, not architecture:\n\n- `op-blob` blobs already carry canonical `PluginSchema` JSON, manifest, D-Bus identity, gRPC descriptor set, methods, subids, and JSON-schema metadata. See [blob.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-blob/src/blob.rs:25) and [blob.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-blob/src/blob.rs:111).\n- Projection still owns an old `SchemaEngine` that writes `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` and `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/*.json`. See [schema_engine.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-projection/src/schema_engine.rs:18).\n- The current projection source also has merge conflict markers inside `write_schemas_to_shm`, so it is not cleanly rebuildable right now. See [schema_engine.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-projection/src/schema_engine.rs:205).\n\nThe catch is bootstrap ordering: projection can read blobs only after something materializes them. Right now the bridge writes blobs only after it already got schemas and registered methods, so using bridge as the only blob writer creates a loop:\n\n`projection needs blobs -> bridge writes blobs -> bridge needs schemas/projection`\n\nSo the clean version is:\n\n`PluginSchema defs -> blob materializer -> /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/*.blob -> projection reads blobs -> D-Bus/GUI/gRPC views`\n\nProjection should become a blob reader/indexer, not the blob authority. The missing component is the first materializer step from real `op-plugins` schemas into SHM blobs.\n\n","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":{"entries":[{"path":"MEMORY.md","lineStart":48,"lineEnd":54,"note":"blob authority and incomplete end to end blob runtime context"},{"path":"MEMORY.md","lineStart":181,"lineEnd":187,"note":"local s6 deploy and validation patterns"}],"rolloutIds":[]}}}
{"timestamp":"2026-07-04T01:40:53.702Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","id":"msg_052f3eefb179c630016a4864a7b09881a2bea3b598d323c862","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"It can. That is probably the right shape.\n\nThe reason it **doesn’t today** is implementation, not architecture:\n\n- `op-blob` blobs already carry canonical `PluginSchema` JSON, manifest, D-Bus identity, gRPC descriptor set, methods, subids, and JSON-schema metadata. See [blob.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-blob/src/blob.rs:25) and [blob.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-blob/src/blob.rs:111).\n- Projection still owns an old `SchemaEngine` that writes `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` and `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/*.json`. See [schema_engine.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-projection/src/schema_engine.rs:18).\n- The current projection source also has merge conflict markers inside `write_schemas_to_shm`, so it is not cleanly rebuildable right now. See [schema_engine.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-projection/src/schema_engine.rs:205).\n\nThe catch is bootstrap ordering: projection can read blobs only after something materializes them. Right now the bridge writes blobs only after it already got schemas and registered methods, so using bridge as the only blob writer creates a loop:\n\n`projection needs blobs -> bridge writes blobs -> bridge needs schemas/projection`\n\nSo the clean version is:\n\n`PluginSchema defs -> blob materializer -> /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/*.blob -> projection reads blobs -> D-Bus/GUI/gRPC views`\n\nProjection should become a blob reader/indexer, not the blob authority. The missing component is the first materializer step from real `op-plugins` schemas into SHM blobs.\n\n<oai-mem-citation>\n<citation_entries>\nMEMORY.md:48-54|note=[blob authority and incomplete end to end blob runtime context]\nMEMORY.md:181-187|note=[local s6 deploy and validation patterns]\n</citation_entries>\n<rollout_ids>\n</rollout_ids>\n</oai-mem-citation>"}],"phase":"final_answer","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f2ac8-99cb-7b71-aed8-af9c80183861"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-07-04T01:41:08.580Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Right. One source of truth: `PluginSchema`.\n\nThe blob is not a second source. It is the sealed runtime form of `PluginSchema`, with schema JSON, manifest, D-Bus identity, gRPC descriptors, methods, and metadata inside it.\n\nSo the correct authority chain is:\n\n`PluginSchema defs -> sealed blob in /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs -> projection/bridge/web read blobs`\n\nNot:\n\n`PluginSchema -> live-schema.json -> bridge makes blobs sometimes`\n\nProjection should only derive views from the blob catalog. If no valid blob exists, the projected entity does not exist. `live-schema.json` should become compatibility output at most, not authority.\n\nThe current repo violates that because projection still writes the old monolith and bridge writes blobs opportunistically. The real fix is one writer/materializer for the blob catalog, then every consumer reads that.\n\n","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":{"entries":[{"path":"MEMORY.md","lineStart":48,"lineEnd":54,"note":"blob authority and incomplete end to end blob runtime context"},{"path":"MEMORY.md","lineStart":181,"lineEnd":187,"note":"local s6 deploy and validation patterns"}],"rolloutIds":[]}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-07-04T01:42:05.953Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes. The blob catalog gives one concrete runtime branch:\n\n`PluginSchema` is authored in code, then sealed once into the blob. After that, projection, bridge, web, MCP, and D-Bus all read the same sealed object identity.\n\nThat removes the split-brain paths:\n\n- no “is `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` newer?”\n- no “did bridge register this schema yet?”\n- no “which bus path did this consumer invent?”\n- no “is projection on old branch logic?”\n- no accidental Btrfs churn from runtime schema writes\n\nThe rule should be simple: if `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/<plugin>.<hash>.blob` is absent or invalid, the object does not exist. Projection becomes a reader/indexer of that catalog, not an alternate schema publisher.\n\n","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":{"entries":[{"path":"MEMORY.md","lineStart":48,"lineEnd":54,"note":"blob authority and incomplete end to end blob runtime context"},{"path":"MEMORY.md","lineStart":181,"lineEnd":187,"note":"local s6 deploy and validation patterns"}],"rolloutIds":[]}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-07-04T01:45:08.666Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes. That is the cleaner design.\n\nThe blobstore should live in SHM as the runtime catalog:\n\n`/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/*.blob`\n\nThen everything reads that catalog:\n\n- projection reads blobs and publishes views\n- bridge reads blobs for reflection/dispatch metadata\n- web/MCP read blobs for schema/UI/tool surfaces\n- no `live-schema.json` authority\n- no branch-dependent projection state\n- no bridge-only side effect deciding what exists\n\nThe only writer should be the schema-to-blob materializer. It takes canonical `PluginSchema` from `op-plugins`, seals the blob, and writes it into the SHM blobstore. After that, consumers are readers.\n\nSo the next code change should be **not** “projection writes blobs.” It should be:\n\n`op-plugins PluginSchema -> op-blob BlobStore::open_shm/write -> /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs`\n\nThen projection changes to read that directory.\n\n","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":{"entries":[{"path":"MEMORY.md","lineStart":48,"lineEnd":54,"note":"blob authority and incomplete end to end blob runtime context"},{"path":"MEMORY.md","lineStart":181,"lineEnd":187,"note":"local s6 deploy and validation patterns"}],"rolloutIds":[]}}}

That is the point of making the blobstore the SHM runtime surface.\n\nThe current blob format already supports that shape:\n\n- section 1: canonical `PluginSchema`\n- section 2: manifest with D-Bus/gRPC/method identity\n- section 3: descriptor bytes\n- section 4: metadata JSON\n\nSo the extension path is straightforward: add typed data sections or expand metadata for runtime state, policy, footprints, Xray headers, model routing, UI render hints, Qdrant refs, etc. Consumers can read one blob and get the whole object contract plus whatever runtime data is valid for that object.\n\nThe important boundary:\n\n`PluginSchema` remains the source of truth for what fields/methods/data are allowed.\n\nThe blobstore is the active runtime image in SHM.\n\nProjection, bridge, web, MCP, Xray config generation, and accountability views can all read that same image instead of reconstructing state from different files.\n\nSo first implementation target is:\n\n`op-plugins schema -> op-blob sealed object -> /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs`\n\nThen we extend blob contents as needed, but the read path stays stable.\n\n","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":{"entries":[{"path":"MEMORY.md","lineStart":48,"lineEnd":54,"note":"blob authority and incomplete end to end blob runtime context"},{"path":"MEMORY.md","lineStart":181,"lineEnd":187,"note":"local s6 deploy and validation patterns"}],"rolloutIds":[]}}}

blobify demo plugins into a catalog dir\n+//! opblob seal-shm                     blobify real plugins into /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs\n+//! opblob seal-plugins <dir>           blobify real plugins demo_seal(Path::new(dir)),\n+        [cmd] if cmd == \"seal-shm\" => seal_plugins(Path::new(DEFAULT_SHM_DIR)),\n+        [cmd, dir] if cmd == \"seal-plugins\" => seal_plugins(Path::new(dir)),\n         [cmd, file] if cmd == \"inspect\" => inspect(Path::new(file)),\n         [cmd, dir] if cmd == \"catalog\" => catalog(Path::new(dir)),\n         [cmd, image, dir] if cmd == \"btrfs-seal\" => btrfs_seal(Path::new(image), Path::new(dir)),\n         [cmd, keyfile] if cmd == \"keygen\" => keygen(Path::new(keyfile)),\n         _ => {\n             eprintln!(\n-                \"usage: opblob demo-seal <dir> | inspect <file.blob> | catalog <dir> | btrfs-seal <image> <dir> | keygen <keyfile>\"\n+                \"usage: opblob demo-seal <dir> | seal-shm | seal-plugins <dir> | inspect <file.blob> | catalog <dir> | btrfs-seal <image> <dir> | keygen <keyfile>\"\n             );\n             return ExitCode::from(2);\n         }\n@@\n     Ok(())\n }\n \n+fn seal_plugins(dir: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {\n+    std::fs::create_dir_all(dir).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n+    let mut cat = ActiveReflectionCatalog::open(dir).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n+    let rt = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()\n+        .enable_all()\n+        .build()\n+        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n+    let registry = DefaultPluginRegistry::new(Arc::new(MemoryStore::new()));\n+    let plugins = rt\n+        .block_on(registry.load_all_plugins())\n+        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n+\n+    let mut sealed = 0usize;\n+    let mut missing_schema = Vec::new();\n+    for plugin in plugins {\n+        let plugin_id = plugin.name().to_string();\n+        let Some(schema) = plugin.schema() else {\n+            missing_schema.push(plugin_id);\n+            continue;\n+        };\n+        let blob = blobify_plugin_schema(&plugin_id, schema);\n+        let path = cat.upsert_blob(&blob).map_err(|e|
