{"timestamp":"2026-07-04T05:47:05.425Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_n8zoIRlBusDTOmagcSXzA5UI","output":"Chunk ID: 281794\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1271\nOutput:\n---\nname: op-dbus-local-s6-deploy\ndescription: Use when the user wants a local deploy/restart in operation-dbus-proto, especially for named binaries/services like op-grpc-bridge-zeroclaw, op-projection, op-dbus-mirror, or op-openvswitch-daemon.\nargument-hint: \"[crate/bin/service targets]\"\ndisable-model-invocation: true\nuser-invocable: false\nallowed-tools:\n  - Read\n  - Grep\n  - Bash\n---\n\n# op-dbus local s6 deploy\n\n## When to use\n\nUse this when the task is \"deploy locally\", \"restart the service\", \"deploy plugins/grpc-bridge/projection\", or similar in `/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto` or a closely related worktree.\n\nDo not use this for:\n- branch push / PR workflows\n- broad host package conversion\n- pure spec/design work with no local build/install/restart\n\n## Inputs / context to gather\n\n1. Confirm the real working tree and branch.\n2. Identify the real deployable targets:\n   - inspect `Cargo.toml` / crate bins\n   - inspect `deploy/s6/<service>/run`\n   - remember `op-plugins` is a library crate, not a deployable binary\n3. Check whether the user wants a broad deploy or a targeted local restart.\n4. Check for host-control constraints:\n   - `sudo -n` availability\n   - `/run/service/<service>` permissions\n   - `/etc/s6/sv/<service>` symlinks back into the repo\n\n## Procedure\n\n1. Map the request to actual `crate:binary:service` targets.\n   - If the name is ambiguous, inspect the repo rather than guessing.\n   - Example: `grpc-bridge` may mean `op-grpc-bridge-zeroclaw`.\n2. Prefer targeted local deploy over broad `deploy/deploy.sh` unless the user explicitly wants the broad path.\n3. Run narrow validation checks first.\n   - `cargo check -p <crate>`\n   - If memory pressure or workspace contention appears, retry with:\n   - `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 cargo check -p <crate> --bin <bin>`\n4. Build the exact release binaries you need.\n   - Example:\n   - `cargo build --release -p op-dbus-mirror --bin ovs-dbus-init -p op-openvswitch-daemon --bin op-openvswitch-daemon`\n5. Install only the target binaries.\n   - `sudo install -m 0755 target/release/<bin> /usr/local/bin/<bin>`\n6. Restart only the matching live services.\n   - `sudo s6-svc -r /run/service/<service>`\n   - If the task is a persistent host service enable/start, use `sudo s6-rc -u change <service>` when appropriate.\n7. Verify with machine-local evidence.\n   - `sudo s6-svstat /run/service/<service>`\n   - `busctl --system list`\n   - `busctl --system introspect <bus-name> <object-path>` when the service should own D-Bus objects\n   - optional: `sha256sum /usr/local/bin/<bin> target/release/<bin>`\n\n## Efficiency plan\n\n1. Read only the specific crate and `deploy/s6/<service>/run` files for the requested targets.\n2. Serialize `cargo check` calls when lock contention is likely.\n3. Use `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1` quickly if a full check gets SIGKILLed or shared dependency compilation is too heavy.\n4. Skip broad deploy scripts if a targeted build/install/restart will satisfy the request.\n5. Stop once install/restart verification succeeds; do not hold the run open on a flaky auxiliary health probe.\n\n## Pitfalls and fixes\n\n- Symptom: `cp -a ... are the same file` from `deploy/deploy.sh`\n  - Likely cause: `/etc/s6/sv/<service>` is a symlink back into the repo checkout.\n  - Fix: detect with `readlink -f` and bypass the broad script; deploy only the requested binaries/services.\n\n- Symptom: `s6-svstat` or `s6-svc` returns `Permission denied`\n  - Likely cause: host service dirs require privilege.\n  - Fix: switch to `sudo -n` immediately.\n\n- Symptom: `cargo check` gets SIGKILLed or hangs in heavy shared deps\n  - Likely cause: memory pressure or too much parallelism.\n  - Fix: use `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1` and narrow to the specific `--bin` target.\n\n- Symptom: health HTTP probe hangs after restart\n  - Likely cause: the probe is not the best readiness gate during service churn.\n  - Fix: rely on `s6-svstat`, D-Bus ownership, and targeted introspection first.\n\n- Symptom: shorthand service request like `crd`\n  - Likely cause: the user expects you to resolve the real service name.\n  - Fix: search `deploy/s6`, `/etc/s6/sv`, and `/run/service` for likely names, then operate on the discovered service.\n\n## Verification checklist\n\n- The requested binary or binaries built successfully.\n- The installed `/usr/local/bin/<bin>` files were updated.\n- The intended `/run/service/<service>` entries report `up` with `sudo s6-svstat`.\n- If the service owns D-Bus objects, `busctl --system list` / `introspect` shows them after restart.\n- No broad deploy-script failure remains in the path actually used.\n\n## Minimal example\n\nFor a local OVS deploy:\n\n```bash\ncargo build --release -p op-dbus-mirror --bin ovs-dbus-init -p op-openvswitch-daemon --bin op-openvswitch-daemon\nsudo install -m 0755 target/release/ovs-dbus-init /usr/local/bin/ovs-dbus-init\nsudo install -m 0755 target/release/op-openvswitch-daemon /usr/local/bin/op-openvswitch-daemon\nsudo s6-svc -r /run/service/op-dbus-mirror\nsudo s6-svc -r /run/service/op-openvswitch-daemon\nsudo s6-svstat /run/service/op-dbus-mirror /run/service/op-openvswitch-daemon\n```\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f2baa-28aa-74f3-a1d2-245f2b619b05"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-07-04T05:50:57.543Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_yd9sLhhWkHZjiZswNTfINWk3","output":"Chunk ID: 898dc8\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1906\nOutput:\n//! Projection Server: pure read-through D-Bus projection of the plugin tree.\n//!\n//! Mounts the projected plugin tree at `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` and serves\n//! each plugin's state as a `ProjectedObject` that reads 1:1 from the shm\n//! projection layer (`/dev/shm/opdbus/projections/<plugin>.json`).\n//!\n//! The MutationEngine (the single write door) writes each plugin's full state\n//! to shm on every mutation. This server mounts the tree from shm on startup\n//! and exposes a `refresh()` D-Bus method on the root interface that re-reads\n//! shm and syncs the tree (mount/unmount). No gRPC subscription, no polling,\n//! no inotify — the tree is derived on demand.\n\nuse anyhow::{Context, Result};\nuse op_projection::*;\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse tracing::{info, warn};\nuse tracing_subscriber::{EnvFilter, FmtSubscriber};\n\n#[tokio::main]\nasync fn main() -> Result<()> {\n    let subscriber = FmtSubscriber::builder()\n        .with_env_filter(EnvFilter::from_default_env())\n        .finish();\n    tracing::subscriber::set_global_default(subscriber)?;\n\n    info!(\"Starting Operation-DBus Projection Server (read-through)\");\n\n    // 1. Initialize Schema Engine + discover plugin schemas (writes to shm).\n    let mut schema_engine = SchemaEngine::new();\n\n    let plugin_reader = match SystemPluginReader::new().await {\n        Ok(reader) => reader,\n        Err(error) => {\n            warn!(\n                error = %error,\n                \"Failed to initialize plugin reader; continuing with empty schema catalog\"\n            );\n            SystemPluginReader::empty()\n        }\n    };\n\n    let projection_schemas = plugin_reader.projection_schemas();\n    let schema_map: HashMap<String, PluginSchema> = projection_schemas\n        .iter()\n        .map(|schema| (schema.name.clone(), schema.clone()))\n        .collect();\n\n    for schema in projection_schemas {\n        register_schema_if_missing(&mut schema_engine, schema)?;\n    }\n\n    info!(\n        schemas = schema_engine.list_schemas().len(),\n        \"Schema catalog published to shm\"\n    );\n\n    // 1b. Seed shm present-state from a boot-time observation of every loaded\n    //     plugin. Mutations (the single write door) overwrite these at runtime;\n    //     this only ensures the projected Data starts from observed reality\n    //     instead of empty defaults.\n    for (plugin_id, state) in plugin_reader.plugin_present_states().await {\n        match serde_json::to_vec(&state) {\n            Ok(bytes) => {\n                if let Err(error) = op_core::projection_shm::write_projection(&plugin_id, &bytes) {\n                    warn!(plugin_id = %plugin_id, error = %error, \"Failed to seed present-state to shm\");\n                }\n            }\n            Err(error) => {\n                warn!(plugin_id = %plugin_id, error = %error, \"Failed to serialize present-state\");\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // 2. Initialize D-Bus server (owns org.opdbus.v1.plugins, root interface\n    //    at /org/opdbus/v1/plugins is always present for introspection).\n    let dbus_server = ProjectionDbusServer::new_with_schemas(schema_map.clone())\n        .await\n        .context(\"failed to start projection D-Bus server\")?;\n\n    // 3. Initial tree sync: mount from shm (mutations) then seed all known\n    //    plugin roots from the schema catalog so the tree is never empty.\n    dbus_server.sync_from_shm().await?;\n\n    let known_plugins: Vec<String> = schema_map.keys().cloned().collect();\n    dbus_server.seed_plugin_roots(&known_plugins).await?;\n\n    let count = dbus_server.object_count().await;\n    info!(\n        objects = count,\n        plugins = known_plugins.len(),\n        \"Initial tree sync complete\"\n    );\n\n    // 4. Initialize JSON-stream server (for WebSocket clients).\n    let mut stream_server = ProjectionStreamServer::new();\n    stream_server.start(8082)?;\n\n    // 5. Run forever. The tree is derived on-demand via the `refresh()` D-Bus\n    //    method on the ProjectionRoot interface. No gRPC, no polling.\n    info!(\"Projection server ready — tree syncs on refresh() D-Bus call or restart\");\n    tokio::signal::ctrl_c().await?;\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn register_schema_if_missing(\n    schema_engine: &mut SchemaEngine,\n    schema: PluginSchema,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    if schema_engine.has_valid_schema(&schema.name) {\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    let schema_name = schema.name.clone();\n    schema_engine\n        .register_schema(schema)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to register projection schema '{}'\", schema_name))?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n    /// Mounted object paths (shared with ProjectionRoot for refresh())\n    objects: Arc<Mutex<HashSet<String>>>,\n    /// Canonical schema catalog passed into D-Bus object creation.\n    schemas: Arc<HashMap<String, PluginSchema>>,\n}\n\nimpl ProjectionDbusServer {\n    pub async fn new() -> Result<Self> {\n        Self::new_with_schemas(HashMap::new()).await\n    }\n\n    pub async fn new_with_schemas(schemas: HashMap<String, PluginSchema>) -> Result<Self> {\n        let objects = Arc::new(Mutex::new(HashSet::new()));\n        let schemas = Arc::new(schemas);\n        let root = {"timestamp":"2026-07-04T05:51:13.287Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_Sump9xmYpk0yMaE88LHnzTGW","output":"Chunk ID: 86a37e\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 670\nOutput:\n\n== /run/service/gbr-wg realpath ==\n/run/s6-rc:s6-rc-init:zakaS1/servicedirs/gbr-wg\n-- /run/s6-rc:s6-rc-init:zakaS1/servicedirs/gbr-wg/run --\n#!/usr/bin/execlineb -S0\nfdmove 1 0\ns6-fdholder-retrieve ../s6rc-fdholder/s \"pipe:s6rc-w-gbr-wg-log\"\nfdswap 0 1\n./run.user $@\n-- /run/s6-rc:s6-rc-init:zakaS1/servicedirs/gbr-wg/run.user --\n#!/bin/sh\n# gbr-wg - WireGuard entry point for GhostBridge privacy chain\n# AGENTS.md: Privacy network uses gbr_* prefix (gbr_wg → gbr_warp → gbr_xray)\n\n# Load WireGuard configuration\nWG_CONF=\"${WG_CONF:-/etc/wireguard/wg0.conf}\"\nIFACE=\"${IFACE:-wg0}\"\n\n# OVS ports (gbr_wg) are created by ovs-attach-ports.sh during boot\n# This service just brings up the WireGuard interface\n\n# Check if config exists\nif [ ! -f \"$WG_CONF\" ]; then\n    echo \"WireGuard config not found: $WG_CONF\"\n    # Exit but tell s6 to not restart immediately\n    exit 0\nfi\n\n# Bring up WireGuard\nexec 2>&1\nexec wg-quick up \"${IFACE}\" && exec pause\n\n== /run/service/opdbus realpath ==\n/run/s6-rc:s6-rc-init:zakaS1/servicedirs/opdbus\n-- /run/s6-rc:s6-rc-init:zakaS1/servicedirs/opdbus/run --\n#!/usr/bin/execlineb -S0\nfdmove 1 0\ns6-fdholder-retrieve ../s6rc-fdholder/s \"pipe:s6rc-w-opdbus-log\"\nfdswap 0 1\n./run.user $@\n-- /run/s6-rc:s6-rc-init:zakaS1/servicedirs/opdbus/run.user --\n#!/bin/sh\nexec 2>&1\n# opdbus - WireGuard identity tunnel to Oracle VPS (10.0.0.2 <-> 10.0.0.1)\n# Gateway IP and iptables are managed by ovsbr0-init\nCONF=\"/etc/wireguard/opdbus.conf\"\nIFACE=\"opdbus\"\n\nif [ ! -f \"$CONF\" ]; then\n    echo \"[opdbus] Config not found: $CONF\"\n    exit 0\nfi\n\n# Bring up the tunnel (Table=off, no auto-routes)\nwg-quick up \"${IFACE}\"\n\n# Add routes manually (Table=off means wg-quick won't add them)\nip route replace 10.0.0.0/24 dev opdbus 2>/dev/null || true\nip route replace 10.0.0.1/32 dev opdbus 2>/dev/null || true\n\n# Refresh identity sled from opdbus interface (tmpfs only — zero-disk rule, Req 7)\n/usr/local/bin/op-identity-sled --iface opdbus --refresh --path /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat 2>/dev/null || true\n\nexec pause\n\n== /run/service/op-projection realpath ==\n/run/s6-rc:s6-rc-init:zakaS1/servicedirs/op-projection\n-- /run/s6-rc:s6-rc-init:zakaS1/servicedirs/op-projection/run --\n#!/usr/bin/execlineb -S0\nfdmove 1 0\ns6-fdholder-retrieve ../s6rc-fdholder/s \"pipe:s6rc-w-op-projection-log\"\nfdswap 0 1\n./run.user $@\n-- /run/s6-rc:s6-rc-init:zakaS1/servicedirs/op-projection/run.user --\n#!/bin/sh\nexec 2>&1\nexport DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=\"${DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS:-unix:path=/run/opdbus/session-bus.sock}\"\nexport OP_DBUS_PROJECTION_BUS=\"${OP_DBUS_PROJECTION_BUS:-session}\"\nexport RUST_LOG=\"${RUST_LOG:-op_projection=info,info}\"\nexec /usr/local/bin/projection_server\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f2baa-28aa-74f3-a1d2-245f2b619b05"}}}

then sudo -n s6-svc -u /run/service/netclient || true; fi\\nif [ -e /run/service/opdbus ]; then\\n  sudo -n rm -f \\\"$(readlink -f /run/service/opdbus)/down\\\" 2>/dev/null || true\\n  sudo -n rm -f /etc/s6/sv/opdbus/down 2>/dev/null || true\\n  sudo -n s6-svc -u /run/service/opdbus || true\\nfi\\nsleep 3\\nfor s in netclient opdbus wg-netmaker gbr-wg gbr-warp wg-decoy wg-opdbus; Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f2bb9-987a-7872-b706-da82f183148c"}}}

Projection Server: pure read-through D-Bus projection of the plugin tree.\n//!\n//! Mounts the projected plugin tree at `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` and serves\n//! each plugin's state as a `ProjectedObject` that reads 1:1 from the shm\n//! projection layer (`/dev/shm/opdbus/projections/<plugin>.json`).\n//!\n//! The MutationEngine (the single write door) writes each plugin's full state\n//! to shm on every mutation. This server mounts the tree from shm on startup\n//! and exposes a `refresh()` D-Bus method on the root interface that re-reads\n//! shm and syncs the tree (mount/unmount). No gRPC subscription, no polling,\n//! no inotify — the tree is derived on demand.\n\nuse anyhow::{Context, Result};\nuse op_projection::*;\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse tracing::{info, warn};\nuse tracing_subscriber::{EnvFilter, FmtSubscriber};\n\n#[tokio::main]\nasync fn main() -> Result<()> {\n    let subscriber = FmtSubscriber::builder()\n        .with_env_filter(EnvFilter::from_default_env())\n        .finish();\n    tracing::subscriber::set_global_default(subscriber)?;\n\n    info!(\"Starting Operation-DBus Projection Server (read-through)\");\n\n    // 1. Initialize Schema Engine + discover plugin schemas (writes to shm).\n    let mut schema_engine = SchemaEngine::new();\n\n    let plugin_reader = match SystemPluginReader::new().await {\n        Ok(reader) => reader,\n        Err(error) => {\n            warn!(\n                error = %error,\n                \"Failed to initialize plugin reader; continuing with empty schema catalog\"\n            );\n            SystemPluginReader::empty()\n        }\n    };\n\n    let projection_schemas = plugin_reader.projection_schemas();\n    let schema_map: HashMap<String, PluginSchema> = projection_schemas\n        .iter()\n        .map(|schema| (schema.name.clone(), schema.clone()))\n        .collect();\n\n    for schema in projection_schemas {\n        register_schema_if_missing(&mut schema_engine, schema)?;\n    }\n\n    info!(\n        schemas = schema_engine.list_schemas().len(),\n        \"Schema catalog published to shm\"\n    );\n\n    // 1b. Seed shm present-state from a boot-time observation of every loaded\n    //     plugin. Mutations (the single write door) overwrite these at runtime;\n    //     this only ensures the projected Data starts from observed reality\n    //     instead of empty defaults.\n    for (plugin_id, state) in plugin_reader.plugin_present_states().await {\n        match serde_json::to_vec(&state) {\n            Ok(bytes) => {\n                if let Err(error) = op_core::projection_shm::write_projection(&plugin_id, &bytes) {\n                    warn!(plugin_id = %plugin_id, error = %error, \"Failed to seed present-state to shm\");\n                }\n            }\n            Err(error) => {\n                warn!(plugin_id = %plugin_id, error = %error, \"Failed to serialize present-state\");\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // 2. Initialize D-Bus server (owns org.opdbus.v1.plugins, root interface\n    //    at /org/opdbus/v1/plugins is always present for introspection).\n    let dbus_server = ProjectionDbusServer::new_with_schemas(schema_map.clone())\n        .await\n        .context(\"failed to start projection D-Bus server\")?;\n\n    // 3. Initial tree sync: mount from shm (mutations) then seed all known\n    //    plugin roots from the schema catalog so the tree is never empty.\n    dbus_server.sync_from_shm().await?;\n\n    let known_plugins: Vec<String> = schema_map.keys().cloned().collect();\n    dbus_server.seed_plugin_roots(&known_plugins).await?;\n\n    let count = dbus_server.object_count().await;\n    info!(\n        objects = count,\n        plugins = known_plugins.len(),\n        \"Initial tree sync complete\"\n    );\n\n    // 4. Initialize JSON-stream server (for WebSocket clients).\n    let mut stream_server = ProjectionStreamServer::new();\n    stream_server.start(8082)?;\n\n    // 5. Run forever. The tree is derived on-demand via the `refresh()` D-Bus\n    //    method on the ProjectionRoot interface. No gRPC, no polling.\n    info!(\"Projection server ready — tree syncs on refresh() D-Bus call or restart\");\n    tokio::signal::ctrl_c().await?;\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn register_schema_if_missing(\n    schema_engine: &mut SchemaEngine,\n    schema: PluginSchema,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    if schema_engine.has_valid_schema(&schema.name) {\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    let schema_name = schema.name.clone();\n    schema_engine\n        .register_schema(schema)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to register projection schema '{}'\", schema_name))?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f2bbe-ec47-74e0-a9dc-ecc14852c333"}}}

This ensures all op-dbus components share the same configuration.\n//!\n//! ## Usage\n//!\n//! Call `load_environment()` early in main() before accessing any config:\n//!\n//! ```rust\n//! use op_core::config::load_environment;\n//!\n//! fn main() {\n//!     load_environment();\n//!     // Now all env vars from /etc/op-dbus/environment are available\n//! }\n//! ```\n\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::path::Path;\nuse tracing::{debug, info, warn};\n\n/// Canonical D-Bus well-known bus name for the op-dbus system.\n///\n/// All components (op-dbus-mirror, projection_server, rovs_proxy, etc.)\n/// must use this constant instead of hardcoding the string.\npub const OPDBUS_BUS_NAME: &str = \"org.opdbus.v1.plugins\";\n\n/// Canonical base object path for the projected plugin tree.\n///\n/// This is the single stable root anchor; plugin leaves live at\n/// `{PLUGIN_BASE_PATH}/<plugin_id>` and must be derived from it (or discovered\n/// by introspection), never hardcoded with a different spelling. Consumers of the mirror's surfaces (OVSDB JSON-RPC,\n/// ObjectManager) dial this name instead.\npub const MIRROR_BUS_NAME: &str = \"org.opdbus.v1.mirror\";\n\n/// Canonical session bus socket path.  No dash — consistent with `opdbus`\n/// used in D-Bus names, object paths, and shm directories.\npub const SESSION_BUS_SOCKET_PATH: &str = \"/run/opdbus/session-bus.sock\";\n\n/// Canonical session bus address string (for `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`).\npub const SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS: &str = \"unix:path=/run/opdbus/session-bus.sock\";\n\n/// Default path for the environment file\npub const DEFAULT_ENV_FILE: &str = \"/etc/op-dbus/environment\";\n\n/// Alternative paths to check (in order of priority)\npub const ENV_FILE_PATHS: &[&str] = &[\"/etc/op-dbus/environment\", \"/etc/op-dbus.env\", \".env\"];\n\n/// Load environment variables from the canonical configuration file.\n///\n/// This function:\n/// 1. Checks `/etc/op-dbus/environment` first (system-wide)\n/// 2. Falls back to `.env` in current directory (development)\n/// 3. Does NOT override existing environment variables\n///\n/// Returns the path that was loaded, or None if no file was found.\npub fn load_environment() -> Option<String> {\n    // Check if a custom path is specified\n    if let Ok(custom_path) = std::env::var(\"OP_ENV_FILE\") {\n        if let Some(path) = try_load_env_file(&custom_path) {\n            return Some(path);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Try each path in order\n    for path in ENV_FILE_PATHS {\n        if let Some(loaded_path) = try_load_env_file(path) {\n            return Some(loaded_path);\n        }\n    }\n\n    debug!(\"No environment file found, using existing environment\");\n    None\n}\n\n/// Try to load an environment file from the given path.\nfn try_load_env_file(path: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    let path_obj = Path::new(path);\n\n    if !path_obj.exists() {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    match fs::read_to_string(path_obj) {\n        Ok(content) => {\n            let mut loaded_count = 0;\n            let mut skipped_count = 0;\n\n            for line in content.lines() {\n                let line = line.trim();\n\n                // Skip comments and empty lines\n                if line.is_empty() || line.starts_with('#') {\n                    continue;\n                }\n\n                // Parse KEY=VALUE\n                if let Some((key, value)) = parse_env_line(line) {\n                    // Don't override existing environment variables\n                    if std::env::var(&key).is_err() {\n                        std::env::set_var(&key, &value);\n                        loaded_count += 1;\n                        debug!(\n                            \"Loaded: {}={}\",\n                            key,\n                            if key.contains(\"KEY\")\n                                || key.contains(\"TOKEN\")\n                                || key.contains(\"SECRET\")\n                            {\n                                \"***\"\n                            } else {\n                                &value\n                            }\n                        );\n                    } else {\n                        skipped_count += 1;\n                        debug!(\"Skipped (already set): {}\", key);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            info!(\n                \"Loaded {} environment variables from {} ({} skipped - already set)\",\n                loaded_count, path, skipped_count\n            );\n\n            Some(path.to_string())\n        }\n        Err(e) => {\n            warn!(\"Failed to read Scribe WireGuard Identity\";\n+\n+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\n+pub struct WgOpdbusPlugin;\n+\n+impl WgOpdbusPlugin {\n+    pub fn new() -> Self {\n+        Self\n+    }\n+}\n+\n+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]\n+#[schemars(extend(\"x-oscal-subid\" = \"sch.network.wg-opdbus.schema@v1\"))]\n+pub struct WgOpdbusState {\n+    #[schemars(extend(\"x-oscal-subid\" = \"src.network.wg-opdbus.interface@v1\"))]\n+    pub interface_name: String,\n+    #[schemars(extend(\"x-oscal-subid\" = \"src.service.wg-opdbus.service@v1\"))]\n+    pub service_name: String,\n+    #[schemars(extend(\"x-oscal-subid\" = \"src.network.wg-opdbus.config@v1\"))]\n+    pub config_path: String,\n+    #[schemars(extend(\"x-oscal-subid\" = \"src.network.wg-opdbus.identity-role@v1\"))]\n+    pub identity_role: String,\n+    #[schemars(extend(\"x-oscal-subid\" = \"obs.network.wg-opdbus.netmaker-separate@v1\"))]\n+    pub netmaker_separate: bool,\n+    #[schemars(extend(\"x-oscal-subid\" = \"obs.network.wg-opdbus.wgcf-present@v1\"))]\n+    pub wgcf_present: bool,\n+}\n+\n+impl Default for WgOpdbusState {\n+    fn {"timestamp":"2026-07-04T06:25:03.416Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_yxWtib4jVHAbV7ymCdZSpCJ1","output":"Chunk ID: 8efdff\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1272\nOutput:\n#!/bin/bash\n# deploy-blob-gemma4.sh\n#\n# Deploys the complete gemma4+zeroclaw \"blob\" as a btrfs subvolume.\n#\n# Architectural reality (per this system):\n# - The **blob itself** is a self-contained btrfs subvolume (or filesystem).\n#   It can be cloned, mounted as a subvol, sent over the wire, or used to extend\n#   other filesystems. This is why btrfs is a big part of the blob story.\n# - **Mutations** (changing live state, configs, etc.) never happen by directly\n#   writing files inside the blob from the running services. All mutation happens\n#   exclusively over D-Bus (zbus), gRPC, and JSON-RPC. This avoids mutation loops.\n# - On host, the gemma4 blob provides a complete, mountable unit containing:\n#     - frozen zeroclaw state + manifests\n#     - the gemma4 model reference / bind\n#     - the recovered PluginObjectBlob / reflection metadata\n#     - any supporting projection files\n#\n# The running zeroclaw surfaces (dbus object + gRPC) project / reflect the blob\n# contents at runtime. The subvolume is the distributable/frozen unit.\n#\n# Incus note: `incus list` on this host is currently authoritative except for\n# the unused \"netmaker-exporter\".\n#\n# Usage:\n#   sudo ./deploy/deploy-blob-gemma4.sh\n#   (or DEST=... BTRFS_ROOT=...)\n\nset -euo pipefail\n\nBLOB_NAME=${1:-zeroclaw-gemma4-gemma4}\nBTRFS_ROOT=${BTRFS_ROOT:-/mnt/btrfs-root}\nSUBVOL=\"@blob-${BLOB_NAME}\"\nDEST=${DEST:-/opt/op-dbus/blobs/${BLOB_NAME}}\n\necho \"=== Gemma4 Zeroclaw Btrfs Blob Deployment ===\"\necho \"Creating btrfs subvolume for the blob (mountable unit): ${SUBVOL}\"\n\nsudo mkdir -p \"$BTRFS_ROOT\"\nif ! sudo btrfs subvolume show \"${BTRFS_ROOT}/${SUBVOL}\" &>/dev/null; then\n  sudo btrfs subvolume create \"${BTRFS_ROOT}/${SUBVOL}\" || true\nfi\n\nsudo mkdir -p \"$DEST\"\nsudo mount --bind \"${BTRFS_ROOT}/${SUBVOL}\" \"$DEST\" 2>/dev/null || true\n\necho \"[blob] subvolume ready at $DEST (btrfs subvol: $SUBVOL)\"\n\n# Live local model requirement\nOLLAMA_URL=${OLLAMA_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:11434}\nMODEL=${MODEL:-gemma4:12b}\n\nif ! curl -fsS --max-time 3 \"$OLLAMA_URL/api/tags\" > /dev/null 2>&1; then\n  echo \"WARNING: Ollama not responding at $OLLAMA_URL (model bind will be recorded anyway)\"\nelse\n  if ! curl -fsS --max-time 5 \"$OLLAMA_URL/api/tags\" | grep -q \"$MODEL\"; then\n    echo \"Pulling $MODEL into host ollama...\"\n    curl -X POST -d \"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"$MODEL\\\"}\" \"$OLLAMA_URL/api/pull\" || true\n  fi\nfi\n\n# Write the contract and snapshot directly into the btrfs-backed blob dir\n# (this is population of the frozen unit, not runtime mutation of live state)\necho \"[blob] writing frozen manifests into the subvol...\"\nsudo tee \"$DEST/MANIFEST.blob.json\" > /dev/null <<'MANIFEST'\n{\n  \"kind\": \"zeroclaw-gemma4-ollama\",\n  \"model\": \"gemma4:12b\",\n  \"provider\": \"ollama\",\n  \"router\": \"gemma4\",\n  \"btrfs_subvol\": \"@blob-zeroclaw-gemma4\",\n  \"note\": \"This directory is the root of a btrfs subvolume. It can be mounted, cloned, or used to extend filesystems. All live mutations to zeroclaw state and routing occur exclusively over D-Bus + gRPC + JSON-RPC. No direct file mutation from the services.\"\n}\nMANIFEST\n\nsudo tee \"$DEST/OBJECT_BLOB.json\" > /dev/null <<'OBJ'\n{\n  \"plugin_id\": \"zeroclaw\",\n  \"schema_version\": \"1.0.0\",\n  \"schema_source\": \"recovered + live PluginSchema from current_state (schemars+uniform)\",\n  \"dbus\": {\n    \"bus_name\": \"org.opdbus.v1.plugins\",\n    \"object_path\": \"/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw\",\n    \"interface_name\": \"org.opdbus.v1.Plugin\"\n  },\n  \"grpc\": {\n    \"package\": \"operation.plugin.v1\",\n    \"service_name\": \"operation.plugin.v1.ZeroclawPluginMethods\"\n  },\n  \"methods\": [\n    {\"schema_name\": \"query_current_state\", \"grpc_name\": \"QueryCurrentState\", \"subid\": \"obs.service.zeroclaw.state\"},\n    {\"schema_name\": \"chat\", \"grpc_name\": \"Chat\", \"subid\": \"mut.service.zeroclaw.chat\"}\n  ],\n  \"gemma4_blob\": {\n    \"model\": \"gemma4:12b\",\n    \"provider\": \"ollama\",\n    \"local_endpoint\": \"http://127.0.0.1:11434\",\n    \"role\": \"context_aware_allocator\",\n    \"mountable_as_subvol\": true\n  }\n}\nOBJ\n\n# Also drop a copy of current declared state for the frozen unit\nsudo tee \"$DEST/state_snapshot.json\" > /dev/null <<'STATE'\n{\"status\":\"active\",\"selected_provider\":\"ollama\",\"selected_model\":\"gemma4\",\"blob\":{\"kind\":\"zeroclaw-gemma4-ollama\",\"status\":\"complete\",\"btrfs\":true}}\nSTATE\n\n# Optionally bind the actual ollama model store (read-only, to keep the blob self-contained without duplication)\nOLLAMA_MODELS=${OLLAMA_MODELS:-/var/lib/ollama/models}\nif [ -d \"$OLLAMA_MODELS\" ]; then\n  sudo mkdir -p \"$DEST/models\"\n  sudo mount --bind --read-only \"$OLLAMA_MODELS\" \"$DEST/models\" 2>/dev/null || true\n  echo \"[blob] models bind-mounted (ro) into subvol\"\nfi\n\necho \"[blob] populated: $DEST\"\necho \"Subvolume can now be mounted elsewhere, cloned (btrfs send/receive), etc.\"\necho \"The live surfaces in zeroclaw (DBus + gRPC) will report this blob as complete when the mount is present.\"\n\necho \"Current incus containers (authoritative except netmaker-exporter):\"\nincus list 2>/dev/null || echo \"incus not available in this context\"\n\nls -l \"$DEST\"\necho\necho \"Blob subvolume ready. Activate / project via normal D-Bus + op-projection paths.\"","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f2bcc-e773-7f00-bcfe-57ac385e3345"}}}

Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. {"timestamp":"2026-07-04T11:22:56.340Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_3u9PouyeixH9lAs0OE1XkRfe","output":"Chunk ID: 2be303\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 870\nOutput:\n//! op-dbus: gRPC server for all Operation services\n//!\n//! Binds to the ovsbr0 interface IPv4 address (discovered at runtime via\n//! rtnetlink) so all Incus containers can reach it through the single OVS\n//! choke point. No hardcoded IP — the address follows whatever ovsbr0 is\n//! assigned.\n//!\n//! Listen address override: `OP_DBUS_GRPC_LISTEN` (e.g. \"0.0.0.0:50051\" for\n//! dev, or an explicit `ip:port`). When unset, op-dbus resolves the first\n//! IPv4 on `OP_DBUS_GRPC_IFACE` (default `ovsbr0`) and binds `<that-ip>:50051`;\n//! if the interface has no IPv4 it falls back to `0.0.0.0:50051`.\n\nuse std::net::SocketAddr;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse tracing::{info, warn};\nuse tracing_subscriber::{EnvFilter, FmtSubscriber};\n\nuse op_grpc_bridge::run_grpc_server;\nuse op_grpc_bridge::MutationEngine;\nuse op_jsonrpc::nonnet::NonNetDb;\nuse op_network::rovs_proxy::OvsdbDbusClient;\nuse op_network::rtnetlink::list_interfaces;\nuse op_state_store::{ChainConfig, EventChain};\nuse tokio::sync::RwLock;\n\n/// Default port when no explicit listen address is supplied.\nconst DEFAULT_GRPC_PORT: u16 = 50051;\n/// Interface whose IPv4 is used for the default bind address.\nconst DEFAULT_GRPC_IFACE: &str = \"ovsbr0\";\n\n/// Resolve the bind address: explicit `OP_DBUS_GRPC_LISTEN` wins; otherwise\n/// discover the first IPv4 on the configured interface and append the port;\n/// otherwise bind all interfaces.\nasync fn resolve_listen_addr() -> SocketAddr {\n    if let Ok(listen) = std::env::var(\"OP_DBUS_GRPC_LISTEN\") {\n        if let Ok(addr) = listen.parse::<SocketAddr>() {\n            return addr;\n        }\n        warn!(%listen, \"OP_DBUS_GRPC_LISTEN did not parse as SocketAddr; falling back to discovery\");\n    }\n\n    let port: u16 = std::env::var(\"OP_DBUS_GRPC_PORT\")\n        .ok()\n        .and_then(|p| p.parse().ok())\n        .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_GRPC_PORT);\n    let iface =\n        std::env::var(\"OP_DBUS_GRPC_IFACE\").unwrap_or_else(|_| DEFAULT_GRPC_IFACE.to_string());\n\n    if let Ok(interfaces) = list_interfaces().await {\n        if let Some(ni) = interfaces.iter().find(|i| i.name == iface) {\n            if let Some(ip) = ni\n                .addresses\n                .iter()\n                .find(|a| a.family == \"AF_INET\" || a.address.parse::<std::net::Ipv4Addr>().is_ok())\n                .and_then(|a| a.address.split('/').next().map(|s| s.to_string()))\n            {\n                if let Ok(addr) = format!(\"{}:{}\", ip, port).parse::<SocketAddr>() {\n                    info!(iface = %iface, %ip, port, \"discovered ovsbr0 bind address\");\n                    return addr;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    warn!(iface = %iface, \"no IPv4 on interface; binding 0.0.0.0\");\n    format!(\"0.0.0.0:{}\", port)\n        .parse()\n        .expect(\"0.0.0.0:port always parses\")\n}\n\n#[tokio::main]\nasync fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n    let filter = EnvFilter::try_from_default_env().unwrap_or_else(|_| EnvFilter::new(\"info\"));\n    let _ = FmtSubscriber::builder()\n        .with_env_filter(filter)\n        .with_target(false)\n        .compact()\n        .try_init();\n\n    let addr = resolve_listen_addr().await;\n\n    let chain = Arc::new(RwLock::new(EventChain::new(ChainConfig::default())));\n    let ovsdb = Arc::new(OvsdbDbusClient::new());\n    let nonnet = Arc::new(NonNetDb::new());\n    let engine = Arc::new(MutationEngine::new(chain, ovsdb, nonnet));\n\n    info!(addr = %addr, \"op-dbus starting\");\n    run_grpc_server(addr, engine, None, None).await?;\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f2cd6-96cf-7862-b313-98dbcd83eb07"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-07-04T11:25:59.549Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_R3lgNEGTOY0n5MLUwqlFnotc","output":"Chunk ID: a1bbaa\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 591\nOutput:\n/// THE STRIKE/ETCH -- single source of truth for the identity footprint.\n///\n/// Blake3( wg_pubkey || schema_catalog_hash(blob-catalog manifest) || mutation_index || source_port ).\n/// source_port is the per-session WireGuard-observed source port (0 when none). It binds the\n/// footprint to the session network context for the accountability loop -- it is NOT an auth\n/// factor (WireGuard is the authenticator; see op-grpc-bridge GhostbridgeInterceptor).\n/// Manifest published by the blob sealer — the ONE place the canonical\n/// `catalog_hash` lives (blake3 leaf-fold over the sealed per-plugin blob\n/// hashes; the blob catalog IS the plugin set).\nconst SHM_BLOB_MANIFEST_PATH: &str = \"/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/.manifest.json\";\n/// Legacy manifest published by op-projection's SchemaEngine; transitional\n/// fallback until every host is re-sealed with the blob-catalog manifest.\nconst SHM_LEGACY_MANIFEST_PATH: &str = \"/dev/shm/opdbus/.manifest.json\";\n/// Legacy derived monolith; last-resort fallback (deploy ordering).\nconst SHM_LIVE_SCHEMA_PATH: &str = \"/dev/shm/live-schema.json\";\n\n/// The single canonical schema-catalog hash (32 bytes), computed ONCE by the\n/// blob sealer and read here — never re-hashed per call site. Reads the blob\n/// catalog manifest's `catalog_hash`; falls back to the legacy SchemaEngine\n/// manifest, then the monolith, on hosts not yet re-sealed. `None` if no\n/// artifact exists.\npub fn schema_catalog_hash() -> Option<[u8; 32]> {\n    for manifest in [SHM_BLOB_MANIFEST_PATH, SHM_LEGACY_MANIFEST_PATH] {\n        if let Ok(bytes) = std::fs::read(manifest) {\n            if let Ok(v) = serde_json::from_slice::<serde_json::Value>(&bytes) {\n                if let Some(hex_str) = v.get(\"catalog_hash\").and_then(|h| h.as_str()) {\n                    if let Ok(raw) = hex::decode(hex_str) {\n                        if let Ok(arr) = <[u8; 32]>::try_from(raw.as_slice()) {\n                            return Some(arr);\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    std::fs::read(SHM_LIVE_SCHEMA_PATH)\n        .ok()\n        .map(|bytes| *blake3::hash(&bytes).as_bytes())\n}\n\npub fn etch_footprint(\n    wireguard_pubkey: &[u8; 32],\n    mutation_index: u64,\n    source_port: u16,\n) -> [u8; 32] {\n    let schema_catalog_hash = schema_catalog_hash().unwrap_or([0u8; 32]);\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f2cd6-96cf-7862-b313-98dbcd83eb07"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-07-04T11:26:51.909Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_2VNYSBMQ8zoxPemOvb6wN9xQ","output":"Chunk ID: 34f697\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 400\nOutput:\n\n/// Promote an `0.0.0.0:PORT` default address to `<wg_ip>:PORT` when the WG\n/// interface is up.  Explicit addresses (not starting with `0.0.0.0:`) are\n/// returned unchanged so env-var or flag overrides always win.\nfn resolve_bind(addr: &str, wg_ip: Option<&str>) -> String {\n    if let Some(rest) = addr.strip_prefix(\"0.0.0.0:\") {\n        if let Some(ip) = wg_ip {\n            return format!(\"{ip}:{rest}\");\n        }\n    }\n    addr.to_string()\n}\n\n/// Resolve bind config (http/grpc addresses, wg_interface) from the\n/// `cognitive_mcp` plugin's live `/dev/shm` projection when present. Falls\n/// back to the already-parsed CLI/env values unchanged, so a cold start\n/// (before the projection is first seeded by op-grpc-bridge) behaves exactly\n/// as it did before this wiring existed.\n///\n/// OSCAL subid: obs.service.cognitive-mcp.bind-config.resolve@v1\nfn cognitive_mcp_bind_config(\n    cli: &Cli,\n) -> op_plugins::state_plugins::cognitive_mcp::CognitiveMcpConfig {\n    use op_plugins::state_plugins::cognitive_mcp::CognitiveMcpConfig;\n\n    op_core::projection_shm::read_projection_bytes(\"cognitive_mcp\")\n        .and_then(|bytes| serde_json::from_slice::<CognitiveMcpConfig>(&bytes).ok())\n        .unwrap_or_else(|| CognitiveMcpConfig {\n            http: cli.http.clone(),\n            grpc: cli.grpc.clone(),\n            wg_interface: cli.wg_interface.clone(),\n            http_enabled: !cli.no_http,\n            grpc_enabled: !cli.no_grpc,\n            dbus_enabled: true,\n        })\n}\n\n#[tokio::main]\nasync fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let cli = Cli::parse();\n\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f2cd6-96cf-7862-b313-98dbcd83eb07"}}}

Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking
